goalDescription: Die lernende Person kann Biases wie Status-quo, Framing oder Anchoring auf Konsumentscheidungen anwenden.
reviewerModel: Codex; exact serving model identifier not exposed
aspectRatioDecision: Close native 16:9 landscape; no exception needed. Existing format not mechanically normalized.

actualInspection.fachlichePruefung: Two visually identical backpacks differ in presentation: one is highlighted and labelled Empfohlen while the other is neutral. Budget and intended hiking use are visible in the shopper thought, making a framing/salience question concrete without claiming a measured bias or an objectively superior product.
actualInspection.phone: At 360 px the identical alternatives, highlighted recommendation label, shopper and budget/use thought remain clear. Side slogans are decorative.
actualInspection.desktop: At 680 px the same backpack features in both frames and the lack of additional product facts make the presentation difference recognizable.
actualInspection.actorPerspective: The shopper looks toward the presented alternatives; no directional document, instrument or notebook is being read.
actualInspection.style: Friendly approachable comic raster, clear broad colors, large conceptual objects; no photorealistic or sterile technical restyling.

interpretationLimits: The illustration invites checking presentation effects. A recommendation label alone does not prove a bias in a particular shopper; the learning text must distinguish framing, salience and other mechanisms using actual decision evidence.
goalTextStatus: Current German competence unchanged in the E2 bilingual candidate; this image review does not attest the positive-evidence profile or bilingual description gate.
